title: Failure-mode: Write tool emitted LITERAL 0x1F from escape-intent — second vector for the invisible-control-char class (Seaworthy e7dd0b)
body: Observation: authoring a test via the file-Write tool, I intended the six-char escape sequence backslash-u001f in a TS template literal; the tool wrote a LITERAL 0x1F byte. Invisible in grep output; broke my own subsequent exact-match Edit (string-not-found on visually identical text). Diagnosis: the editing-tool layer itself is a vector for the 4fd66dc5 class — escape-intent can materialise as raw bytes, so 'I typed the escape' is not proof the file holds the escape. Cure: od -c as tiebreaker (per existing doctrine); perl -pe 's/\x1f/<escape>/g' to convert; post-Write byte-verify any file where a control-char escape was intended. Pointer: keyword-view.integration.test.ts in oak-wt-airy-g (cured in working tree, lands with G4b c2); prior instance event 4fd66dc5.
